सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 कैसे भरें? (How to Apply Online)

हर साल लाखों उम्मीदवार सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 भरने की प्रक्रिया में गलतियाँ कर बैठते हैं, जिससे उनका आवेदन रद्द हो सकता है। नीचे दी गई सरल प्रक्रिया से आप अपना फॉर्म सही तरीके से भर सकते हैं।

आवेदन की चरणबद्ध प्रक्रिया

  1. संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना (Notification PDF) ध्यान से पढ़ें और अपनी पात्रता जांचें।
  2. वैध ईमेल आईडी और मोबाइल नंबर से पोर्टल पर पंजीकरण (Registration) करें।
  3. व्यक्तिगत विवरण, शैक्षणिक योग्यता, और आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें (फोटो, हस्ताक्षर, प्रमाणपत्र)।
  4. निर्धारित आवेदन शुल्क का ऑनलाइन भुगतान करें और भुगतान की रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।
  5. फॉर्म सबमिट करने से पहले सभी जानकारी की दोबारा जांच करें और फॉर्म का प्रिंटआउट अवश्य लें।

What is the last date for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026?

Where can I apply for Anganwadi jobs online in 2026?

Forest Guard Recruitment 2026 - Latest Vacancies & Eligibility

Forest Guard recruitment is suitable for candidates interested in forest protection, patrolling and field-level government work. Forest Guard vacancies are generally announced by state forest departments or authorized recruitment boards.

What does a Forest Guard do?

A Forest Guard helps protect forest areas, monitor activities, assist with wildlife conservation and report suspected forest offences. Duties can include patrolling assigned forest areas and supporting senior forest officials.

What is the qualification for Forest Guard Recruitment 2026?

Some Forest Guard recruitments require Class 10 or Class 12 qualifications from a recognized board. However, the exact educational requirements depend on the state and recruitment notification.

Candidates should check:

  • Education: Required qualification and recognized board.
  • Age Limit: Minimum and maximum age, including the age-calculation date.
  • Physical Standards: Height, chest measurements or other applicable requirements.
  • Selection Process: Written examination, physical tests or other notified stages.
  • Vacancies: Total and category-wise posts.
  • Application Dates: Registration opening and closing dates.

How can I apply for Forest Guard Vacancy 2026?

Find the Forest Guard recruitment in the vacancy table above, open the detailed notification, confirm eligibility and follow the official application instructions.

Candidates should apply only through the website or submission method prescribed by the recruiting authority.

Forest Range Officer Recruitment 2026 - RFO Jobs

Forest Range Officer Recruitment 2026 provides opportunities for candidates interested in forest administration, conservation and supervisory roles.

A Forest Range Officer, also referred to as a Range Forest Officer or RFO in some recruitment systems, may oversee forest protection activities, supervise field staff and manage responsibilities within an assigned forest range.

What is the qualification for Forest Range Officer recruitment?

Forest Range Officer recruitment generally involves graduate-level eligibility. Some notifications require degrees in specified subjects such as science, agriculture, forestry or other approved disciplines.

The accepted qualifications vary by recruiting organization. A graduation degree alone does not automatically make a candidate eligible for every RFO vacancy.

How are Forest Range Officers selected?

Depending on the recruitment rules, selection may include:

  • Preliminary or main written examinations
  • Physical standards or fitness assessments
  • Interviews, where prescribed
  • Document verification
  • Medical examination

Candidates searching for RFO Vacancy 2026, Forest Ranger Recruitment or Forest Range Service Officer notifications should check the relevant vacancy details for exact eligibility and selection stages.

Physical standards and fitness assessments are common in certain field-level posts, particularly Forest Guard and some officer-level recruitment.

However, not every Forest Department post has a physical test. Technical, administrative and other positions may follow different selection procedures.

Where physical testing is required, the official notification specifies the standards, test format and qualifying conditions.

Forest Department Recruitment 2026 - Frequently Asked Questions

1. Is Forest Department Recruitment 2026 open?

Forest-related vacancies are announced throughout the year by different recruiting organizations. Check the latest vacancy table above for the status of individual recruitments. An advertised post should be considered open only within its confirmed application period.

2. What is the last date for Forest Department Recruitment 2026?

The last date differs for each recruitment. Check the applicable notification's closing date in the table and verify it against the official announcement.

3. How can I apply for Forest Guard Recruitment 2026?

Find an applicable Forest Guard vacancy, review the educational and physical requirements, and follow the official application instructions before the closing date.

4. Can 10th-pass candidates apply for Forest Department jobs?

Some Forest Guard, Forest Watcher and support recruitments may accept Class 10 qualifications. Eligibility depends on the post and recruiting authority.

5. Can 12th-pass candidates apply for Forest Guard vacancies?

Yes, some Forest Guard recruitments accept Class 12 qualifications. Check the specific notification to confirm any subject or additional eligibility requirements.

6. Can graduates apply for Forest Range Officer recruitment?

Graduates may qualify for certain Forest Range Officer vacancies, but some recruitments require degrees in specified disciplines. Candidates must verify the accepted qualifications.

7. Is a physical test required for Forest Guard recruitment?

Many Forest Guard recruitments include physical standards or fitness tests. The exact requirements depend on the recruiting authority.

8. What is the age limit for Forest Guard recruitment?

The age limit varies by state and notification. Check the official minimum and maximum ages, cut-off date and applicable relaxations.

9. Is there an exam for Forest Department jobs?

Many Forest Guard, Forester and officer-level recruitments include written examinations. Other roles may use different selection methods. Follow the official selection process for the chosen vacancy.

10. What is the difference between a Forest Guard and a Forest Range Officer?

A Forest Guard generally performs field-level protection and monitoring duties. A Forest Range Officer usually carries supervisory and administrative responsibilities for a forest range. Exact duties differ under the relevant service rules.

11. Can ex-servicemen apply for Forest Department recruitment?

Eligible ex-servicemen can apply for vacancies where they meet the recruitment requirements. Reservation benefits and relaxations depend on the applicable rules.

12. Are Forest Department jobs available in every state?

Different states announce vacancies at different times. Not every state or post necessarily has an active recruitment notification at any given moment.

13. Is there a single apply online link for all Forest Department vacancies?

No. Each recruiting organization may use a different application portal or offline application process.

Open the relevant recruitment from the latest vacancy table and follow its official notification link.

Note: Apprenticeship posts (under the Apprentices Act) are not regular government jobs but are a popular no-exam entry route into PSUs and railways for ITI/diploma/graduate candidates, offering valuable hands-on experience.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

J&K Bank Recruitment 2026: Jammu & Kashmir Bank Limited has released two detailed recruitment notifications for 1,053 Banking Associate and Probationary Officer vacancies. These include 1,033 Banking Associate posts for domiciles of the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir and 20 Probationary Officer posts for domiciles of the Union Territory of Ladakh. Candidates with a Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognized university can apply, subject to the respective domicile and age requirements. The basic age limit is 20 to 30 years as on 1 January 2026, with category-specific relaxation and an additional special age concession for the Ladakh PO recruitment. Online applications are accepted from 7 November to 26 November 2026 through the Careers section of jkb.bank.in.

The JK Bank Banking Associate Recruitment 2026 selection is based on a single online examination conducted by IBPS, while JK Bank Probationary Officer Recruitment 2026 requires a Preliminary Examination, Main Examination and Interview. The starting basic pay is Rs. 24,050 for Banking Associates and Rs. 48,480 for Probationary Officers. Candidates must read the respective notification carefully, as J&K domicile holders are eligible for the Banking Associate recruitment and Ladakh domicile holders are eligible for the Probationary Officer recruitment covered by these advertisements.

Both notifications have the same application and fee-payment window. Candidates should monitor the Careers section of J&K Bank's official website for examination dates, call letters and subsequent updates.

Post Name Eligible Domicile Vacancies
Banking Associate Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir 1033

Important Domicile Rule: The two advertisements apply to different Union Territories. Only candidates holding the required J&K domicile are eligible for the Banking Associate recruitment. Only candidates holding the required Ladakh domicile are eligible for the Probationary Officer recruitment in the uploaded notification.

Reservation will be implemented according to the applicable rules of the respective Union Territory. The notifications provide reservation percentages but do not publish a complete category-wise allocation of the 1,033 and 20 vacancies.

J&K Bank Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Educational Qualification

Both posts require a Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a university recognized by the Government of India or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Central Government or UGC.

Post Required Qualification
Banking Associate Graduation in Any Discipline
Probationary Officer Graduation in Any Discipline

Candidates must possess a valid graduation marksheet or degree certificate by 26 November 2026, the last date of online registration.

Applicants must enter their graduation marks percentage while applying. Candidates whose universities award CGPA or OGPA must convert their grades into percentages according to the university's official conversion formula and provide documentary proof when required.

Can Final-Year Students Apply for J&K Bank Recruitment 2026?

Final-year students who have not completed their graduation by 26 November 2026 do not satisfy the prescribed qualification cut-off. Candidates must have documentary proof that they are graduates by the registration closing date.

Is a Domicile Certificate Mandatory?

Yes. The recruitment is restricted to candidates domiciled in the respective Union Territory.

Post Domicile Requirement
Banking Associate UT of Jammu & Kashmir Domicile
Probationary Officer UT of Ladakh Domicile

Selected candidates must submit a valid domicile certificate issued by the competent authority during the prescribed verification process.

J&K Bank Recruitment 2026 Age Limit

The base age limit for both Banking Associate and Probationary Officer is 20 to 30 years as on 1 January 2026, before applicable relaxation.

This includes eligible unreserved and reserved-category candidates.

The total permissible relaxation is subject to the condition that the candidate's maximum age does not exceed 56 years. Applicants should apply the stated relaxation rules to their actual category and date of birth.

Separate application fees are prescribed for Banking Associate and Probationary Officer recruitment. All stated fees are exclusive of GST and applicable bank transaction charges.

Last Date for Fee Payment: 26 November 2026.

The application fee is non-refundable. Registration is considered complete only after successful online fee payment.

J&K Bank Banking Associate Selection Process 2026

The Banking Associate recruitment involves an online examination conducted by IBPS, followed by provisional selection and document verification according to the bank's recruitment rules.

The notification does not prescribe a separate interview or Main Examination for Banking Associates.

Reasoning Ability 35 40 20 Minutes
Total 100 100 60 Minutes

Exam Language: English.

Negative Marking: One-fourth of the marks assigned to an incorrectly answered question will be deducted.

Candidates must qualify in each section and meet the overall cut-off decided by IBPS in concurrence with J&K Bank.

Banking Associate Minimum Qualifying Marks

Candidates domiciled in J&K who successfully completed apprenticeship training with J&K Bank will be awarded additional marks equal to 2.5% of the maximum marks in the online examination, as prescribed by the notification.

For the 100-mark online examination, this corresponds to 2.5 marks. This benefit is separate from the additional one-year age relaxation available to eligible former bank apprentices.

J&K Bank Probationary Officer Selection Process 2026

The Probationary Officer recruitment consists of three stages:

  1. Preliminary Online Examination.
  2. Main Online Examination, including Objective and Descriptive Papers.
  3. Personal Interview.

Shortlisting to the Main Examination is generally limited to ten times the vacancies in each category, while shortlisting for interview is limited to three times the vacancies in each category, subject to the bank's recruitment provisions.

J&K Bank PO Preliminary Exam Pattern

Subject Questions Marks Duration
English Language 30 30 20 Minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 35 30 20 Minutes
Reasoning Ability 35 40 20 Minutes
Total 100 100 60 Minutes

The Preliminary Examination is conducted in English and has separately timed sections.

Minimum Aggregate Qualifying Marks: 40% for General Category and 35% for reserved categories, subject to overall merit and sectional cut-offs.

J&K Bank PO Main Exam Pattern

Important: The PO Main Examination includes a descriptive paper assessing essay writing and comprehension, potentially covering economic, social, banking, technology, ethics and current-affairs topics.

Negative marking of one-fourth of the marks assigned to each incorrect objective question applies to both Preliminary and Main Examinations.

Qualifying Marks - Reserved Categories 35%

Final Merit Weightage - Interview 20%

Final merit will be calculated using the Main Examination and Interview in an 80:20 ratio. Candidates must qualify in both stages.

Preliminary Examination marks are used for shortlisting and do not form part of the final merit calculation.

Indian Bank Apprentice Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must hold a graduate degree in any discipline from a recognized university or an equivalent qualification recognized by the Central Government. Graduation must have been completed within the period specified by the bank.

Indian Bank Apprentice Educational Qualification

Important Graduation Year Restriction: Candidates who completed graduation before 1 April 2022 are not eligible. Candidates whose graduation results were declared after 1 November 2026 are also not eligible.

Can Graduates from 2021 Apply?

No. Candidates who passed graduation before 1 April 2022 do not satisfy the passing-date requirement under the FY 2026-27 apprenticeship notification.

Can Final-Year Students Apply?

Only candidates whose final graduation result was declared on or before 1 November 2026 meet the notified qualification cut-off. Candidates awaiting their final result after that date are not eligible.

Previous Apprenticeship and Work Experience Restrictions

The bank does not permit applications from candidates who have already undergone apprenticeship training, are currently undergoing apprenticeship training or had their apprenticeship terminated due to their own fault.

Candidates who have accumulated one year or more of work experience after completing their educational qualification are also ineligible.

Indian Bank Apprentice Age Limit 2026

The age limit for Indian Bank Apprentice Recruitment 2026 is 20 to 28 years as on 1 November 2026, with applicable relaxation for eligible categories.

Indian Bank Apprentice Stipend 2026

Selected apprentices will receive a monthly stipend of Rs. 15,000 in Metro/Urban branches or Rs. 12,300 in Rural/Semi-Urban branches during the 12-month training period.

The apprenticeship duration is 12 months of on-the-job training under the Apprentices Act, 1961.

Indian Bank Apprentice Leave and Certification Rules

Apprentices are entitled to bank holidays and one casual leave after completing each month of training. A maximum of four casual leaves may be taken at one time.

The notification requires more than 338 paid days during the 12-month period to become eligible for the Certificate of Proficiency, subject to the prescribed assessment and completion conditions.

After successful training and assessment, the Board of Apprenticeship Training (Southern Region) will issue a digital Certificate of Proficiency through NATS 2.0.

Is Indian Bank Apprenticeship a Permanent Job?

No. Apprenticeship is a fixed-duration training arrangement. Indian Bank has no obligation to provide regular or contractual employment after completion of training, and apprentices do not have a right to claim employment with the bank.

Indian Bank Apprentice Application Fee 2026

The application fee is Rs. 800 plus GST for General, OBC and EWS candidates. SC, ST and PwBD candidates must pay Rs. 175 plus GST.

The application fee is non-refundable. Applicable bank transaction charges are additional.

Indian Bank Apprentice Selection Process 2026

The selection procedure includes an online objective examination and a Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT). Indian Bank may also conduct an interview at its discretion.

  1. NATS Registration: Eligible candidates complete their apprenticeship registration and profile.
  2. Online Application: Candidates submit the application and pay the applicable fee.
  3. Online Written Test: Candidates appear in the 100-mark objective examination.
  4. Local Language Proficiency Test: Qualified candidates must demonstrate proficiency in the selected State/UT language unless exempt.
  5. Interview, If Conducted: The bank may include or dispense with an interview.
  6. Merit List: Candidates are ranked according to the applicable State/UT and category-wise merit rules.
  7. Document Verification: Eligibility and supporting certificates are verified.
  8. Medical Fitness: Engagement is subject to the bank's prescribed medical fitness requirements.
  9. Apprenticeship Contract: Selected candidates receive their digital engagement through NATS 2.0.

Indian Bank Apprentice Exam Pattern 2026

The online examination consists of 100 multiple-choice questions carrying 100 marks, with a composite duration of 60 minutes.

Indian Bank Apprentice Exam Qualifying Marks

Indian Bank will determine the minimum qualifying marks on the aggregate examination score. There are no separate minimum qualifying marks for individual sections.

SC, ST, OBC and PwBD candidates receive a 5% relaxation in the prescribed aggregate qualifying percentage.

How Is the Indian Bank Apprentice Merit List Prepared?

The bank will prepare merit lists State/UT-wise and category-wise according to online examination performance.

Candidates will be ranked in descending order of aggregate marks. If candidates have identical marks at the cut-off, the older candidate will receive preference.

Where examinations are conducted in multiple sessions, scores will be normalized using the equi-percentile method.

A State/UT-wise and category-wise waiting list may also be prepared to fill unoccupied apprenticeship seats.

Indian Bank Apprentice Local Language Test 2026

Candidates must be able to read, write, speak and understand one of the specified local languages of their selected State or Union Territory.

The Local Language Proficiency Test will be conducted after the online examination. Candidates who fail to qualify will not be engaged as apprentices.

Who Is Exempt from the Indian Bank Local Language Test?

Candidates who provide Class 8, Class 10 or Class 12 marksheets or certificates proving they studied their selected local language are exempt from appearing in the Local Language Proficiency Test.

Important: Candidates without the prescribed language-study evidence must qualify in the LLPT. The test will be held at a centre decided by the bank in the relevant State/UT, and candidates must bear their own travel expenses.

Indian Bank Apprentice State and District Preference 2026

Applicants can apply for only one State or Union Territory. During registration, candidates may choose three preferred districts within the selected State/UT.

The bank gives the applicant's resident district the first preference in the applicable merit arrangement, while candidates may select two additional neighbouring districts.

Important: District preferences do not guarantee posting in a particular branch or district. Indian Bank may allot candidates to any district within their selected State/UT according to availability and operational requirements.

Eligible candidates can apply for the 1,500 Indian Bank apprenticeship training seats from 5 November to 25 November 2026.

Apply Online: Click Here

Indian Bank Careers: Indian Bank Official Recruitment Website

Application Last Date: 25 November 2026.

Important: Candidates must complete their NATS profile fully and submit the Indian Bank apprenticeship application. Merely registering on NATS without completing the recruitment-specific application is not sufficient.

How to Apply Online for Indian Bank Apprentice Recruitment 2026?

Step 1 - Register on NATS 2.0

  1. Visit the official NATS website at nats.education.gov.in.
  2. Open the Student Registration facility.
  3. Complete the enrolment process using the information requested on the portal.
  4. Enter accurate personal, contact and educational qualification details.
  5. Provide graduation passing information and other required certificates.
  6. Complete all mandatory profile sections until the NATS profile shows 100% completion.
  7. Save the generated NATS Enrolment ID.

Step 2 - Apply for Indian Bank Apprenticeship 2026

  1. Visit Indian Bank Careers or the NATS portal.
  2. Locate the recruitment titled Engagement of Apprentices in Indian Bank - 2026.
  3. Read the detailed advertisement and verify the qualification, graduation passing date, age and experience restrictions.
  4. Open the corresponding online application facility.
  5. Click New Registration if registering for the recruitment for the first time.
  6. Enter your name, contact details and email address.
  7. Note the provisional registration number and password.
  8. Use the Save and Next facility while completing the application.
  9. Enter the required personal, address, graduation and category details.
  10. Select one eligible State/UT.
  11. Choose the preferred districts within that State/UT.
  12. Select one of the prescribed local languages for the language proficiency requirement.
  13. Upload the photograph, signature, left thumb impression and handwritten declaration.
  14. Complete the additional details requested by the application form.
  15. Open the Preview tab and carefully verify all entered information.
  16. Select Complete Registration after confirming the details.
  17. Pay the applicable fee through the online payment facility.
  18. Complete the application by 25 November 2026.
  19. Save the application printout and payment confirmation for future reference.

Important: Once the application is finally submitted, changes to the submitted details will not be permitted. Candidates should ensure that their name, date of birth and educational details match their official certificates.

Documents Required for Indian Bank Apprentice Recruitment 2026

Candidates should keep the following documents and records available for registration, application and subsequent verification, as applicable.

  • Graduation degree certificate and marksheets.
  • Proof showing the graduation result was declared on or before 1 November 2026.
  • Date-of-birth proof.
  • Valid identity proof.
  • NATS 2.0 Enrolment ID.
  • Recent passport-size colour photograph.
  • Scanned signature.
  • Left thumb impression.
  • Handwritten declaration.
  • SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS category certificate, if applicable.
  • PwBD disability certificate or UDID card, where applicable.
  • Class 8, 10 or 12 certificate showing study of the selected local language, if claiming LLPT exemption.
  • Other applicable documents requested by the bank during verification.

Documents must be uploaded in the prescribed JPG/JPEG format. Candidates must also capture a live photograph through a webcam or mobile phone using the application portal's facility.

Indian Bank Apprentice Handwritten Declaration 2026

The handwritten declaration must be written in English on white paper using black ink. It must be written in the candidate's own handwriting and must not be written entirely in capital letters.

The official declaration is:

I, _______ (Name of the candidate), hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required.

Candidates should reproduce the declaration exactly as prescribed in Annexure II of the official notification.

Indian Bank Apprentice Exam Centres 2026

The online examination will be conducted at various centres across India. The tentative examination centre list is provided in Annexure I of the official advertisement.

Candidates can indicate their preferred examination centre while applying, subject to the options provided by the application form. However, Indian Bank may allot a different centre according to availability.

Requests for examination centre changes will not be entertained. Candidates must bear their own examination-related travel expenses.

Indian Bank Apprentice Admit Card 2026

Indian Bank will issue examination call letters through its official website or other recruitment-related portals identified in the notification.

Candidates must download their call letters using the registration number or roll number and the required login credentials.

Call letters will not be sent by post. Applicants should regularly check their registered email and the official bank recruitment website for examination updates.

Indian Bank Apprentice Certificate and Contract Conditions

Selected candidates will receive a digital apprenticeship engagement offer through NATS 2.0. The apprenticeship contract is normally for 12 months and terminates automatically after completion of the prescribed training period.

Candidates must report at the allotted bank branch or training venue on the specified joining date. Failure to report may lead to termination of the apprenticeship contract.

Early Termination of Apprenticeship

The advertisement specifies conditions for early termination of the apprenticeship contract, including voluntary withdrawal, misconduct, employment elsewhere and medical inability to continue training.

A candidate who voluntarily leaves the training before completing the contract may be required to pay an amount equivalent to one month's stipend, under the notified conditions.

Separate provisions apply to termination after securing gainful employment or due to medical grounds. Candidates should read the full contractual conditions before accepting the apprenticeship.

Indian Bank Apprentice Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions

  • Indian Bank has announced 1,500 apprenticeship training seats for FY 2026-27.
  • Online applications are open from 5 November to 25 November 2026.
  • Graduation in any discipline is required.
  • Graduation must have been completed between 1 April 2022 and 1 November 2026.
  • The age limit is 20 to 28 years as on 1 November 2026, with applicable relaxation.
  • Candidates with one year or more of post-qualification work experience are not eligible.
  • Applicants who have already undergone apprenticeship training are ineligible.
  • Only one State/UT can be selected.
  • Candidates must maintain a fully completed NATS 2.0 profile.
  • The application fee is Rs. 800 or Rs. 175 plus GST, depending on category.
  • Selection includes a 100-mark online test and Local Language Proficiency Test.
  • The bank may conduct an interview at its discretion.
  • Local language exemption is available with the prescribed school-study evidence.
  • The stipend depends on whether the allotted branch is Metro/Urban or Rural/Semi-Urban.
  • Training lasts for 12 months.
  • Apprenticeship does not guarantee regular or contractual employment.
  • Ex-Servicemen and Disabled Ex-Servicemen are not eligible under the notification.
  • Candidates must satisfy document verification and medical fitness requirements.
  • The bank may revise the training seats, selection requirements or schedule through official updates.

SBI Manager (Security) Experience Requirements

Candidates applying for Manager (Security) in MMGS-III must satisfy either of the following conditions:

  • An officer not below the rank of Major in the Indian Army or equivalent rank in the Indian Navy or Air Force, with at least 10 years of commissioned service.
  • An officer not below the rank of Deputy Commandant in paramilitary forces, with at least 10 years of service as an officer in the force.

SBI Deputy Manager (Security) Experience Requirements

  • An officer not below the rank of Assistant Commandant in paramilitary forces, with at least 5 years of service as an officer in the force.

SBI SO Selection Process 2026

The selection process consists of an online written examination followed by a personal interview. The final merit calculation gives 70% weightage to Professional Knowledge and 30% to the interview.

  1. Online Written Test: Candidates appear in the objective examination.
  2. Shortlisting: SBI shortlists candidates based on the examination results and applicable requirements.
  3. Personal Interview: Shortlisted candidates attend an interview carrying 100 marks.
  4. Document Verification: Educational qualifications, service experience, medical fitness and category certificates are verified.
  5. Final Merit List: Prepared using normalized Professional Knowledge and interview marks.

SBI reserves the right to modify the selection process, including considering shortlisting followed by interview, if required.

  • Marks obtained in these three qualifying sections are not counted toward final merit.
  • Candidates must obtain the minimum qualifying marks fixed by SBI in the applicable sections.
  • Professional Knowledge carries 100 marks and contributes to final merit.
  • There is no negative marking for incorrect answers.

SBI Security Officer Job Responsibilities

Selected Manager and Deputy Manager (Security) officers will be responsible for improving security arrangements at SBI branches and offices.

  • Conduct periodic security audits of branches and offices.
  • Review existing security arrangements and recommend improvements.
  • Organize security drills, lectures and employee awareness programmes.
  • Monitor security systems and reduce incidents caused by security lapses.
  • Support implementation of disaster management plans.
  • Visit branches and other administrative units to assess security requirements.
  • Coordinate with civil, military, police and other Government authorities.
  • Perform additional security administration duties assigned by SBI.

Selected officers may be posted or transferred to SBI offices anywhere in India according to the Bank's requirements.

RRB ALP CBAT Re-Exam Date 2026 - 12 November

The RRB ALP CBAT re-examination is scheduled for 12 November 2026 in the third shift. The re-examination has been arranged for specified candidates affected by the postponement of their earlier CBAT or by technical problems during the examination conducted on 30 October 2026.

The re-examination is not a fresh aptitude test for every ALP applicant. Only candidates covered by the official rescheduling notice or individually identified for re-examination should follow the revised schedule.

Who Is Eligible for RRB ALP CBAT Re-Exam 2026?

The rescheduled examination notice identifies two broad groups of affected candidates.

1. Candidates from Postponed CBAT Test Centres

Some CBAT examinations were postponed because of unforeseen circumstances at specific test centres. Candidates originally allotted to those affected sessions are covered by the rescheduled examination arrangements.

Test Centre Code City
9417 Visakhapatnam
9208 Visakhapatnam
7954 Rajahmundry
30677 Delhi

Candidates should compare the test-centre code on their earlier CBAT e-call letter with the codes identified in the rescheduling notice.

2. Candidates Affected by Technical Problems

Certain candidates who appeared in the CBAT on 30 October 2026 experienced technical problems that affected their test. The Railway Recruitment Boards have released identified the affected candidates after reviewing the examination records.

These candidates are being informed individually through their registered email addresses. Candidates should follow the official communication and the instructions issued for their re-examination.

How to Download RRB ALP CBAT Re-Exam City Slip 2026?

Candidates covered by the CBAT re-examination can check their exam city and date through the authorised railway examination-login facility.

  1. Visit the official website of your respective Railway Recruitment Board.
  2. Open the recruitment section for CEN 01/2025 - Assistant Loco Pilot.
  3. Find the CBAT re-examination city and date intimation link.
  4. Click the authorised candidate-login link.
  5. Enter your Registration Number and the Date of Birth or other credentials requested by the portal.
  6. Complete the security verification displayed on the login page.
  7. Submit your details to access the examination city information.
  8. Check your allotted examination date, city and other displayed details.
  9. Download or save the city intimation slip if the portal provides that option.
  10. Download your CBAT e-call letter separately when it becomes available.

Check RRB ALP CBAT Re-Exam City Intimation Slip 2026

RRB ALP CBAT Re-Exam Admit Card 2026

The RRB ALP CBAT Re-Exam Admit Card 2026, also called the e-call letter, is separate from the examination city intimation slip.

Under the official ALP recruitment instructions, e-call letters are generally made available approximately four days before the examination date. For the 12 November re-examination, this indicates availability around 8 November 2026, subject to the actual portal activation.

Particulars Status
Re-Exam Date 12 November 2026
City Intimation Slip Released on 5 November
Expected E-Call Letter Availability Around 8 November 2026

Difference Between RRB ALP City Slip and Admit Card 2026

The RRB ALP city intimation slip and admit card serve different purposes. Candidates should not confuse the availability of their city slip with the release of the complete examination e-call letter.

City Intimation Slip CBAT Admit Card / E-Call Letter
Informs candidates about examination city and date Provides examination-entry information and instructions
Helps with travel planning Required for examination-centre entry
Generally released earlier Generally released about four days before examination
Does not replace the admit card Must be carried according to RRB instructions

RRB ALP CBAT Vision Certificate 2026

The RRB ALP recruitment includes important vision-certificate requirements. The rescheduled CBAT notice reportedly distinguishes between candidates whose original examination was postponed and candidates offered another examination opportunity because of technical problems.

Candidate Group Vision Certificate Requirement
Candidates from the four postponed test centres Original Vision Certificate in the prescribed Annexure VI-A format required
Candidates individually offered re-examination because of technical problems Notice reports an exemption for this group

Candidates subject to the vision-certificate requirement must use the prescribed format under CEN 01/2025. The certificate should bear the required attestation from an Eye Specialist, including the specified professional identification information.

Important: Candidates must verify the group-specific exemption and certificate instructions from the official re-examination notice. They should not assume that the same rule applies to every candidate appearing on 12 November 2026.

RRB ALP CBAT Re-Exam 2026 - Which Attempt Will Be Considered?

The rescheduled examination guidance reports specific evaluation rules for candidates who are being offered another attempt because of technical problems during the 30 October 2026 test.

For such candidates, appearing in the 12 November re-examination means that the re-examination performance will be considered in place of the earlier attempt. Candidates who choose not to appear may be evaluated using their original 30 October performance, according to the conditions stated in the rescheduling notice.

These provisions are particularly important for candidates eligible for a repeat attempt. They should read the exact official notice before deciding whether to attend.

RRB ALP CBAT SC/ST Travel Authority 2026

Eligible SC/ST candidates may be entitled to a free travel authority under the recruitment rules. The relevant travel facility is made available through the designated official examination portal.

Candidates claiming this facility should check their eligibility, download the required travel document and follow the railway booking instructions. The original community certificate and prescribed identity proof may be required during travel verification.

RRB ALP CBAT Re-Exam Day Instructions 2026

Candidates appearing in the rescheduled CBAT should check their e-call letters and the relevant recruitment notice carefully before attending the examination.

  • Confirm that you are eligible for the re-examination.
  • Check the allotted examination city and date.
  • Download the CBAT e-call letter when available.
  • Verify the exact examination centre and reporting time.
  • Carry the original photo identity document required by RRB.
  • Carry the prescribed vision certificate if applicable to your candidate group.
  • Keep the required photograph and other documents ready according to the e-call letter.
  • Follow the instructions regarding prohibited items and identity verification.
  • Report within the time permitted for examination-centre entry.

RRB ALP Selection Process 2026

The Assistant Loco Pilot recruitment under CEN 01/2025 follows multiple examination and verification stages. The latest city-slip announcement relates specifically to the CBAT stage.

Stage Selection Process
Stage 1 First Stage Computer-Based Test (CBT-1)
Stage 2 Second Stage Computer-Based Test (CBT-2)
Stage 3 Computer-Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
Stage 4 Document Verification
Stage 5 Medical Examination

The release of the CBAT city intimation slip does not constitute a declaration of aptitude-test results or final selection.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

RRB Isolated Category Recruitment 2026: Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), under the Ministry of Railways, Government of India, have released Centralised Employment Notification (CEN) No. 09/2026 for 191 vacancies in seven isolated-category posts. The recruitment includes Junior Translator (Hindi), Chief Law Assistant, Public Prosecutor, Senior Publicity Inspector, Staff and Welfare Inspector, Scientific Assistant (Training) and Lab Assistant Grade III (Chemist & Metallurgist). Candidates with the prescribed 12th Science, Bachelor's degree, postgraduate degree or professional qualifications can apply according to the selected post. The age limit ranges from 18 to 30 years and 18 to 40 years, depending on the post, as on 1 January 2027. Initial basic pay ranges from Rs. 19,900 to Rs. 44,900 under the 7th CPC. Online applications are open from 5 November to 4 December 2026 through rrbapply.gov.in.

Important: Candidates can apply to only one Railway Recruitment Board under CEN 09/2026. Multiple applications to the same or different RRBs will result in rejection and possible debarment. Applicants must possess the prescribed educational qualification by 4 December 2026 and satisfy the post-specific medical standards. Candidates awaiting final qualification results are not eligible.

RRB Isolated Category Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

The educational qualification differs substantially across the seven posts. Applicants must meet the specific academic and professional requirements listed in Annexure A by 4 December 2026.

Post Name Essential Qualification

Chief Law Assistant Eligibility

Candidates must possess a university degree in Law and have at least three years of standing practice as a Pleader at Bar.

Serving Railway employees with a Law degree may also apply if they have completed at least five years of service in any branch of Railway Administration, subject to the notification's conditions.

Public Prosecutor Eligibility

Applicants must have a recognized Bachelor's degree in Law and five years of standing as an Advocate at Bar.

Important: A Law degree alone is not sufficient. The prescribed professional practice requirement must also be satisfied.

Senior Publicity Inspector Eligibility

Candidates need a recognized university degree together with a Diploma in Public Relations, Advertising, Journalism or Mass Communication from a recognized institution or university.

Two years of experience in a relevant field is desirable, not mandatory.

RRB Junior Translator (Hindi) Eligibility 2026

Junior Translator applicants must satisfy one of the prescribed Master's degree language combinations involving Hindi and English, along with an additional translation qualification or experience.

The academic requirement may be fulfilled through a recognized Master's degree in Hindi or English with the other language as a compulsory/elective subject or medium of examination at degree level, or through the alternative Master's degree language combinations specified in Annexure A.

In addition, candidates must possess either:

  • A recognized Diploma or Certificate Course in translation from Hindi to English and vice versa; or
  • Two years of translation experience between Hindi and English in Central or State Government offices, including Government of India undertakings.

Important: A general Master's degree or Hindi/English language proficiency alone does not automatically satisfy this post's eligibility conditions.

Staff and Welfare Inspector Eligibility

Applicants must have graduation along with at least one of the following qualifications:

  • Diploma in Labour or Social Welfare.
  • Diploma in Labour Laws.
  • LLB with papers in Labour Laws.
  • Postgraduate Diploma in Personnel Management.
  • MBA with papers in Personnel Management.
  • MBA in Human Resources.
  • Postgraduate Diploma in Human Resource Management with relevant Personnel Management papers from a Government-recognized institution.

Scientific Assistant (Training) Eligibility

Candidates must possess a Master's degree in Psychology with at least 50% marks in aggregate.

Specialization in Industrial, Organisational or Clinical Psychology; experience in counselling or guidance programmes; and working computer knowledge are desirable qualifications.

RRB Lab Assistant Grade III Eligibility

Candidates must have passed Class 12 (+2 Stage) or an equivalent examination with Physics and Chemistry as subjects.

This is the only post category in CEN 09/2026 for which the stated essential educational qualification is at the 12th-standard level.

Can Final-Year Students Apply?

No. Candidates awaiting their final examination results for the prescribed essential qualification are not eligible. The required qualification must have been obtained by 4 December 2026.

Difference Between EBC and EWS in Railway Recruitment

Economically Backward Class (EBC) candidates may qualify for examination fee concession where their annual family income is below Rs. 50,000 and they satisfy the documentary requirements.

Economically Weaker Section (EWS) is a separate category used for reservation under applicable Government rules.

Claiming EBC fee concession does not automatically provide EWS reservation or an OBC benefit.

RRB Isolated Category Selection Process 2026

The recruitment involves a single-stage Computer Based Test (CBT), followed by a Translation Test for Junior Translator candidates, where applicable, and subsequent Document Verification and Medical Examination.

  1. Computer Based Test: Eligible candidates appear for the prescribed objective examination.
  2. Translation Test: Junior Translator (Hindi) candidates shortlisted from CBT must qualify in the translation test.
  3. Document Verification: Candidates are shortlisted according to merit, vacancy availability and applicable reservation rules.
  4. Medical Examination: Candidates must meet the medical standards applicable to their selected post.
  5. Final Empanelment: Subject to merit, qualifications, medical fitness and successful verification.

RRBs reserve the right to conduct additional recruitment stages where necessary under the notification.

How to Calculate SSC CGL Tier 1 Marks Using Answer Key 2026?

Candidates can estimate their Tier-I raw marks by comparing their responses with the provisional answer key and applying the official marking scheme.

SSC CGL Tier-I Raw Score = (Correct Answers × 2) – (Incorrect Answers × 0.50)

For example, if a candidate has 75 correct answers, 15 incorrect answers and 10 unattempted questions, the estimated raw score would be:

(75 × 2) – (15 × 0.50) = 142.50 marks

The calculated score is only an estimate. SSC may apply normalisation for examinations conducted in multiple shifts, and accepted objections may affect the final evaluation.

The SSC CGL Tier-I examination was conducted across multiple dates and shifts. The official recruitment notification provides for normalisation of examination scores where multiple shifts are conducted.

Candidates should understand that the raw marks calculated using the provisional answer key may differ from the normalised marks used by SSC for determining merit and applicable cut-off marks.

Final assessment will depend on SSC's officially prescribed evaluation and normalisation procedures.

Candidates qualifying the Tier-I examination according to the applicable criteria will be considered for the next stage, Tier-II. The Commission will publish the result and relevant cut-off information through its official website.

Pay only the amount displayed on the objection portal at the time of submission, and keep the payment confirmation until the final answer key is published.

What to Attach or Mention as Proof

Support each objection with a clear justification and a reference, such as a page from a standard NCERT or SCERT textbook. A specific reference is more useful to the review than a general statement that the answer is wrong.

How to Calculate Your Probable Score Using the UP Special TET Answer Key

  1. Download the key for your paper and your booklet series.
  2. Compare each of your marked answers with the provisional key.
  3. Award 1 mark for every correct answer.
  4. Do not deduct marks for wrong or unattempted questions, as there is no negative marking.
  5. Add up the marks. Your total is out of 150.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Check the answer key of your own paper and your own booklet series only.
  • Raise objections only within the window, which ends on 12 November 2026.
  • Give a specific justification and reference for every objection.
  • Check the fee shown on the portal before paying, and save the payment receipt and objection summary.
  • Use only the official UPESSC website. Do not enter login details on any other page.
  • Treat your probable score as an estimate until the final answer key and result are published.

Provisional Answer Key vs Final Answer Key

The provisional key was released on 5 October 2026 so candidates could compare their answers and raise objections. After reviewing the objections, GSSSB issued the final key. The final key carries corrections for some questions based on expert review and supporting documents submitted by candidates.

  • Provisional key: Open to objections and meant for an estimated score.
  • Final key: Reflects the board's review and is the reference for evaluation.
  • Changed questions: The final key lists the Question ID, the earlier answer and the corrected answer for each affected question across shifts and dates. The total number of changed questions is Not Available Officially in this article.

If you calculated your score from the provisional key, recheck it against the final key, because even a few corrected questions can change your total.

Both papers are offline, pen-and-paper, objective-type (multiple choice), and set entirely in English. The written examination totals 500 marks, and qualifiers are called for a 100-mark Personality Test.

UPSC CMS 2026 Marking Scheme

  • Each question has four alternative answers.
  • One-third (0.33) of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for a wrong answer.
  • Marking more than one answer to a question is treated as a wrong answer, even if one of the marked options is correct the same penalty applies.
  • A question left blank/unattempted carries no penalty.

  2. Go to the "Examinations" or "What's New" section on the homepage.
  3. Click the link for "Combined Medical Services Examination, 2026 – Provisional Answer Key."
  4. Select and open the Paper I or Paper II PDF as needed.
  5. Download the PDF and match it against your response sheet / marked options.

How to Raise an Objection Against the UPSC CMS Answer Key 2026

UPSC accepts representations against the question paper and provisional answer keys only through its official online portal no email, post, or in-person submissions are entertained.

  1. Log in at upsconline.nic.in using your registered credentials.
  2. Go to "Examinations" and select "Representations on Question Paper & Provisional Answer Keys."
  3. Choose the relevant question, paper, and reason for objection.
  4. Submit supporting justification where the portal allows it.
  5. Submit before the window closes  6:00 PM on the 7th day from the exam date. Nothing is entertained after this deadline.
